newsitem.title: DENMARK: Year-end buying takes Danish shares to new highs.
newsitem.headline: Year-end buying takes Danish shares to new highs.

text.p: Danish share prices closed at a new record high on Monday, the last trading day before the three-day Christmas break.
Dealers said that the wave of buying was encouraged by the fact that today's transactions are not booked until January 2.
"They're taking an advance on next year's budget, but even so the level of activity was quite surprising," a trader said.

The KFX top-20 index rose 1.22 point to 133.37, in overall bourse turnover of 1.14 billion crowns, beating the record of 132.34 set on December 10. Its March future rose 0.05 point to 133.90, with 10 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.

Den Danske Bank set a personal record, closing 11 crowns higher at 468 and beating its December 20 high of 459. Rival Unidanmark gained five crowns to 304 and third-largest bank BG Bank rose two crowns to 274.
Tele Danmark and Danisco climbed four crowns each, closing at 317 and 354 crowns respectively.
Outside the top 20, East Asiatic Company rose eight crowns to 118 on news that it had signed an Asian and African marketing agreement with Eastman Kodak.
The market re-opens on Friday, December 27. Claus Mathisen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969651
